# A handler inside a view loop reads the loop's own variable, on bubbletea.
#
# Every head form a focusable loop can take is here, because the focus cursor
# is an int ordinal and each head answers "which iteration is this?"
# differently. A map head is not among them: the checker refuses a map loop in
# a view body, since a map fixes no order for the ordinal to name.
#
# Whether the handler reads the element varies from loop to loop, and Go
# rejects the binding it does not read. The unread name here is one the
# rendered body happens to spell inside another word -- `it` inside `hits` --
# which is what a substring test over the rendered Go cannot tell from a
# reference.
#
# This has to be a compiled run: the interpreter never emits either loop, so
# `--platform none` passes under the bug.

[!exec:go] skip 'go toolchain required'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"
import app "sngl:app"

output { go { bubbletea } }

component main ui {
    var items list<string> = ["a", "b"]
    var picked = ""
    var hits = 0

    vbox {
        for var it = items {
            button(text=it, @click { picked = it })
        }
        for items {
            button(text="any", @click { hits += 1 })
        }
        for var i, it = items {
            button(text=it, @click { picked = "{i}:{it}" })
        }
        for var i, it = items {
            button(text=it, @click { hits += i })
        }
    }
    text(value=picked)
}

func testStartsEmpty(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.picked == "")
    t.assert(c.hits == 0)
}

app.window {
    main
}
